messages.content: How long will it take to paint the Eiffel Tower?

message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower would be a massive undertaking. The tower stands at 330 m (including its antennas) and has roughly 18 000 square metres of exposed metal surface. Even if you had a crew of 100 painters working full‑time (8 h days, 5 days a week), you’d still be looking at several months just for the actual application of paint—assuming you could work continuously without weather delays or safety constraints.

In practice, the French Ministry of Culture and the company responsible for the tower’s maintenance schedule repainting in phases over a few weeks each year, typically during the winter when fewer tourists visit. A complete overhaul of all visible surfaces usually takes about 2–3 months of active work, but the entire project—including planning, procurement, safety inspections, and post‑painting inspections—can stretch over a year or more.
